verdict: Avoid for now — lend only to USFDA-clean, low-concentration API/formulation units with tight covenants; skip small CRO-dependent and single-customer borrowers.
title: Aurangabad Pharmaceuticals & APIs: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**A pharma unit here converts imported and domestic raw materials into APIs and finished dosages, and the cash comes back only after a regulatory-cleared batch ships and the buyer pays.** The plant is the asset; the USFDA inspection status is the real collateral. Aurangabad (Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar) hosts large names — Lupin received an EIR for its facility after a September 1–5, 2025 pre-approval inspection [3], and Glenmark's Aurangabad unit completed a USFDA inspection [2]. Both are dated late 2025, so treat them as background, not current proof.

## Where value and cash sit
**Value sits in approved product registrations and customer contracts, not in the building; cash sits in receivables and inventory, and that is where the strain shows.** Peer rating work shows the pattern: Concord Biotech's working capital intensity was 52% in FY2019, 47% in FY2020 and 48% in 7MFY2021, down from 77% in FY2018, and still called high [10]. Cohance Lifesciences had operating cash flows of ₹200 crore in FY24 with term loans of ₹152 crore and fund-based limits of ₹420 crore, utilisation easing from 70-90% to 40-50% in Q1FY25 [9]. So when a proposal lands, check receivable days and inventory holding first; if the buyer list is short, ask for the top-customer share.

## What has changed now
**The national demand signal is weak while bank credit is running far ahead of output, so pricing power is thin and lenders are competing for the same good names.** India-wide output is -2.1% Apr-to-date against bank credit +21.6% YoY, a gap of +23.7 pp [D]. Maharashtra electricity demand grew 6.0% Apr-to-date, 3.5 pp slower than India's 9.5% [D], while state GST collections grew 8.6% against India's 6.1% [D]. The data-based call is AVOID at 36 [D]. **Read this as: the sector is not in a downturn, but the marginal borrower is.**

## Where to grow, and how to grow safely
**Pursue mid-size API and CDMO units with a clean USFDA record and diversified buyers; avoid small contract-research-dependent firms and single-customer units.** Peers show the upside: Aarti Pharmalabs posted record quarterly revenue of ₹613 crore, up 47% YoY, with EBITDA of ₹136 crore and margin at 22.2% [4][6]; RPG Life Sciences targets 25% API growth and is evaluating another acquisition within 12 months [5], though its stock fell over 10% after Q2 despite revenue rising 16.5% to ₹211.6 crore [7]. A small rated company with ₹61.0 crore FY2024 revenue was hit by weak US contract-research demand and carries high customer concentration [8]. Structure as working-capital-led facilities with a term loan only against a specific approved-product capex; take monthly stock-and-receivable statements, quarterly regulatory-status confirmation, and annual audited financials.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch the regulatory calendar and the buyer list, not the topline.** A USFDA observation or import alert at a borrower's plant is an immediate stop — Wockhardt hit a 52-week low on a UK import alert [1]. Falling limit utilisation alongside rising receivables means the buyer is stretching; rising inventory with flat sales means batch rejections.
watch: observation or import alert -> freeze new limits, review existing
receivable days rising with flat sales -> ask for buyer-wise ageing
utilisation falling while receivables rise -> seek explanation, tighten drawing power
inventory up with flat sales -> cut limit, inspect stock statement
